n: The first of five closing ‘Hallelujah’ psalms (146–150), each beginning and ending with ‘Praise ye the LORD.’ The psalmist urges his own soul to praise.

f.w: Praise the LORD, O my soul

n: He will praise God for as long as he lives and breathes.
Don’t put your ultimate trust in rulers or in any mortal — they cannot save.

f.w: Put not your trust in princes

n: When a person’s breath leaves, they return to the ground, and all their plans die with them. A wordplay: ‘man’ (adam) returns to ‘earth’ (adamah).
True happiness belongs to the one whose help is the God of Jacob and whose hope is in the Lord.

f.w: the God of Jacob for his help

n: This God made heaven, earth, sea, and everything in them — and he keeps faith forever, unlike mortal princes.
He brings justice to the oppressed, food to the hungry, and freedom to prisoners. Jesus’ ministry fulfilled these very works.
He opens blind eyes, lifts up the bowed-down, and loves the righteous — works Jesus did during his ministry in Israel and among the Nephites.

f.w: openeth the eyes of the blind
raiseth them that are bowed down

n: He protects foreigners and supports orphans and widows — society’s most vulnerable — but turns the path of the wicked into a dead end.
Unlike mortal rulers who die, the Lord reigns forever — Zion’s God for every generation. Hallelujah!

f.w: The LORD shall reign for ever
